clue.text: Swindle just instigated by theatrical rogue

indicators.note: something just instigated has only begun, so only the opening letter of the word swindle is used

parts.note: camp means theatrical, exaggerated in manner

explanation.surface: A con trick devised by a stagey villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swindle' tempts you towards SCAM, but only its first letter is wanted; 'by' just joins it to CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rascal, a mild synonym for a rogue.

clue.text: Contents of minimal archive, one behind another

explanation.surface: A compressed folder holding a lone document, items queued in order.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is computing: an archive with the minimum contents holds one file.
explanation.definitionFit: Single file is an idiom for a line of people one behind another; the first sense is a sole document.

clue.text: Publish piece of music

explanation.surface: Releasing a song to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: To air something is to make it public or broadcast it; an air is also a tune or melody.

clue.text: Lyrical writer given habitual response

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
a tic is a habitual involuntary twitch or response

explanation.surface: A songwriter who always replies the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic means having the expressive, lyrical quality of poetry.

clue.text: Get lift round German town, heading for the border

indicators.note: one piece is placed round the others, so it encloses them

parts.note: to hitch is to get a lift from passing drivers
Ems (Bad Ems) is a spa town in Germany

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, taken here from the word the

explanation.surface: Thumbing a ride around a German town on the way to the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for the border' reads as travelling to the frontier, but 'heading for' takes the first letter of 'the', and 'border' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemstitch is a decorative stitch used to finish the border or hem of fabric, so the sewing term names a kind of border.

clue.text: Run the bar, suffering indigestion

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked about or distressed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A landlord running a pub with a stomach upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartburn is a burning pain behind the breastbone caused by indigestion.

clue.text: Writing about princess and king

indicators.note: one piece is put about the other, enclosing it

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
Ida is the princess of Gilbert and Sullivan's Princess Ida

explanation.surface: A document concerning a princess and a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'princess' tempts DI; here it is IDA, giving M-IDA-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Midas is the legendary king of Phrygia whose touch turned everything to gold.

clue.text: Before playing, cellist must acknowledge applause

explanation.surface: Advice for a concert cellist: pick up the bow, and later bask in the clapping.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal: a cellist must pick up a bow to play.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a bow is to bend forward to acknowledge applause; a cellist literally takes a bow before playing.

clue.text: In the course of criminal activity, I dropped down dead, almost — that's absurd!

indicators.note: dropped down means the letter falls to a lower place, here later in the word

parts.note: thievery is criminal activity, stealing

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word dead loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A preposterous tale of collapsing in the middle of a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: Take THIEVERY plus DEA (dead 'almost'); the I of THIEVERY is 'dropped down' to stand before DEA, giving THEVERY-IDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The very idea! is an exclamation of indignant disbelief, a way of saying that's absurd.

clue.text: Fell into harbour

explanation.surface: Someone tumbled into a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a verb; it is the noun meaning an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell is an animal's skin or pelt, as is a hide; to harbour a fugitive is to hide them.

clue.text: Childminder styled, in USA, "minder'

indicators.note: styled means arranged or fashioned, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An American's word for a carer of children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'styled' rearranges USA together with MINDER; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after young children, a childminder.

clue.text: Speaker's requirement for work

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard, so the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a need is a requirement

explanation.surface: What a public speaker needs in order to do the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work dough or clay with the hands, pressing and folding it.

clue.text: Make presentable coat mum's left in a pile, wrinkled

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, so it sits inside it
wrinkled suggests something crumpled out of shape, so these letters are rearranged
mum has left the coat, so her letters are removed from it

parts.note: a mackintosh is a raincoat
Ma is a familiar word for mum

explanation.surface: A tidy-up: Mum's abandoned coat lies crumpled on a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: Take MA from MACKINTOSH to leave CKINTOSH, then put it in LIAPE, the letters of 'a pile' rearranged ('wrinkled'), as LI-CKINTOSH-APE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lick into shape is an idiom for putting something in good order, making it fit to be seen.

clue.text: Start fighting about order, mistakenly below cost

indicators.note: one piece goes about the other, surrounding it
done mistakenly means done wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Customers come to blows over an order wrongly priced too cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of 'below cost' go about OM: C-OM-ETOBLOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to blows is an idiom for starting a physical fight.

clue.text: Top film comedian nearly finished popular book

parts.note: best means top, finest

indicators.note: the name is nearly finished, so it stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: Peter Sellers was a British film comedian

explanation.surface: A leading screen comic all but completed a hit novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly finished' cuts the last letter off SELLERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestseller is a book that sells in very large numbers, a popular book.

clue.text: Note or two

parts.note: two notes of the sol-fa scale, the first of them fa
the second of the two notes is me (also spelt mi)

explanation.surface: Asking for a single musical note, or perhaps a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' first reads as a musical note; it is the definition in its sense of renown, while 'two' gives a pair of sol-fa notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Note can mean distinction or renown, as in a person of note, which is fame.

clue.text: Grace's runny honey's pure

indicators.note: something runny flows out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that a woman's liquid honey is unadulterated.
explanation.walkthrough: Euphrosyne is one of the Three Graces of Greek myth; the possessive 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphrosyne, goddess of mirth, is one of the three Graces (Charites) of Greek mythology.

clue.text: Vehicle taking sportsman over the course

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another comes before it

parts.note: a half (half-back) is a player in football or rugby
a track is a racecourse

explanation.surface: A vehicle carrying an athlete across the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-track is a military vehicle with wheels at the front and caterpillar tracks behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-track is a vehicle with front wheels and rear caterpillar tracks, often military.

clue.text: Turning up during race, little woman's companion

indicators.note: one piece comes during the other, placed inside it

parts.note: a plate is a horse race run for a prize

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A girl who shows up in the middle of a race with her friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reverses the girl's name, which then goes 'during' the race; a plate is a race run for a trophy, and Amy March is the youngest of the Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a friend to play with, a companion.

clue.text: Miss Trent left it to give information about Leonard

indicators.note: one piece goes about another, enclosing it

parts.note: to tell is to give information
Len is a short form of the name Leonard

explanation.surface: A woman leaves something for someone else to report on a man.
explanation.walkthrough: TELL goes about LEN to make T-LEN-ELL. Little Nell, whose surname is Trent, is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Nell Trent is the child heroine of Dickens's novel, generally called by her nickname Little Nell.

clue.text: Correct reversal of flow

indicators.note: the word is turned around, so its letters are read from the end

parts.note: tide is the flow of the sea

explanation.surface: A statement that the ebb is the true turning of the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to correct it, fixing errors before publication.

clue.text: Solitary island has appeal

parts.note: Herm is one of the Channel Islands
it is sex appeal, as in the it girl

explanation.surface: A lonely island that still holds attractions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solitary' is a noun here: a recluse.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary, as a noun, is someone who lives alone in seclusion, which is a hermit.

clue.text: Only understood by tanned people? Unacceptable

explanation.surface: A remark that something is grasped only by the sunburnt, and outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally: something beyond pale people, comprehensible only to those with a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond the pale is an idiom for conduct outside the bounds of decency; the cryptic half splits it as past those who are pale.

clue.text: Girl not quite all there

indicators.note: not quite means falling short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to be all there is to be normal, mentally sound

explanation.surface: A woman who seems a little scatterbrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a girl's name, a typical crossword use.

clue.text: Told to put a stop to certain parties getting together?

indicators.note: told means spoken out, so a word said the same way is meant

parts.note: to block is to put a stop to something

explanation.surface: Being told to stop some groups from merging.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of parties or nations combined for a common purpose.

clue.text: Sponge, a dessert making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a fool is a dessert of fruit and cream

explanation.surface: A sponge pudding returning to favour as a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' looks like a cake beside 'dessert', but it is the bath sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofa is a bath sponge made from the dried fibrous inside of a gourd.

clue.text: Dream a lot about The Stones?

indicators.note: about here means in a jumbled order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan daydreams constantly about the Rolling Stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Stones' suggests the rock band; the definition refers to stones used for roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Road metal is broken stone used in making or repairing roads, so the stones are an example of it.

clue.text: Quotation of Greta Garbo's

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the letters sit inside the words

explanation.surface: A famous line from the actress Greta Garbo.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across greTA Garbo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag is a familiar quotation or saying, such as a Latin tag.

clue.text: About to check vessel showing sign of class

parts.note: ca, for circa, is the abbreviation for about
to stem is to check or stop a flow
an ark is a vessel, like Noah's

explanation.surface: Someone is about to inspect a ship that displays its rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to check' looks like a phrase of intention, but 'About' gives CA and 'check' gives STEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste mark is a symbol on the forehead indicating a Hindu's caste, a sign of social class.

clue.text: Row about grand cat

indicators.note: one piece is put about the other, surrounding it

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: An argument over a fine feline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel; it means a line, TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is the largest of the big cats.
